code.label: churn model: training and scoring SQL

lines.text: CREATE MODEL churn OPTIONS(model_type='logistic_reg') AS SELECT * FROM prepared_training_view
SELECT * FROM ML.PREDICT(MODEL churn, TABLE customers)
CREATE MODEL churn TRANSFORM(ML.STANDARD_SCALER(tenure_months) OVER () AS tenure,
ML.ONE_HOT_ENCODER(plan) OVER () AS plan, churned) OPTIONS(...) AS SELECT * FROM raw_training
SELECT * FROM ML.PREDICT(MODEL churn, TABLE customers)
SELECT * FROM ML.PREDICT(MODEL churn, (SELECT ... copied scaling from the training view, with this month's mean ...))
SELECT * FROM ML.PREDICT(MODEL churn, TABLE customers) WHERE predicted_churn_probs > 0.99

brief.situation: You own the churn model at Pellow Mobile (fictional). It was trained in BigQuery ML on a prepared view where tenure was scaled and plan type one-hot encoded by hand in SQL. This month's scoring job calls ML.PREDICT on the raw customers table. It says 94% of customers will churn. The offer list goes to the mailer at 12:00. It is 11:05.
handover: The training view did the scaling and encoding in SQL; nobody copied it into the scoring job.
The mailer can send at most 40,000 offers.
howItWorks: Pick a step from the action list: look, change, check or ship. Nothing you pick is typed or executed: every step shows an authored result.
Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
Shipping is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the retention lead: why scores were wrong, what you changed, and how you know.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: The model was trained on tenure scaled and plan one-hot encoded in a SQL view; scoring passed raw months and text, so inputs no longer meant what the model learned.

parts.label: What you changed
parts.criteria: Retrained with a TRANSFORM clause so BigQuery ML applies the same preprocessing during ML.PREDICT; copying the SQL drifts; a higher threshold keeps meaningless scores.
parts.modelAnswer: TRANSFORM with scaler and one-hot encoder.

parts.criteria: Holdout AUC and the predicted churn rate match last quarter.

scoring.modelReasoning: A churn rate of 94% against 6% last quarter points at inputs, not customers. The model was trained on scaled tenure and one-hot encoded plans from a view, but scoring passes raw columns. Retrain with a TRANSFORM clause so the same preprocessing is stored in the model and applied by ML.PREDICT, then check the holdout and the churn rate. Copying the SQL into scoring drifts; a higher cut-off over wrong scores picks an arbitrary list.
